triples.evidence_text: Cyclobenzaprine is a prescription muscle relaxant used short-term to relieve muscle spasms caused by sprains, strains, and injuries, including low back and neck pain. It is used together with rest and physical therapy to help relieve the pain, tenderness, and limited movement caused by muscle spasm. 1,2

Cyclobenzaprine is also used to treat fibromyalgia in adults, where it can help reduce pain. For fibromyalgia, it is taken as a sublingual (under the tongue) tablet at bedtime under the brand name Tonmya. In clinical trials, Tonmya significantly reduced fibromyalgia pain compared with placebo over 14 weeks, and close to half of treated patients achieved at least a 30% improvement in pain. 3

triples.entity_2: muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease

qualifiers.examples: cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease

triples.evidence_text: Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain that drive muscle tone and spasm, which allows tight, overactive muscles to relax. It acts within the central nervous system, primarily at the level of the brain stem, and does not act on the muscles themselves or at the junction between nerves and muscle. 1,2 Because cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease, such as cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease. 1,2
The way cyclobenzaprine works in fibromyalgia is not known. Laboratory studies show it blocks several receptor types, including serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors. 3

triples.section_title: Is cyclobenzaprine a controlled substance or narcotic?
triples.evidence_text: No. Cyclobenzaprine is not a controlled substance and is not a narcotic, opioid, or benzodiazepine. It is a skeletal muscle relaxant that is chemically related to tricyclic antidepressants, and its FDA labeling states directly that cyclobenzaprine is not a controlled substance. 3

qualifiers.co_medications: certain antidepressants, tramadol, bupropion, meperidine or verapamil

triples.evidence_text: Serotonin syndrome. Cyclobenzaprine can cause a serious condition called serotonin syndrome when taken with certain other medicines, especially antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics), tramadol, bupropion, meperidine, and verapamil. Get medical help right away if you have agitation, hallucinations, fever, sweating, shivering, fast heart rate, muscle stiffness or twitching, loss of coordination, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. 1,2,3

triples.entity_2: the two weeks before conception and the first trimester of pregnancy

qualifiers.reason: animal data suggest neural tube defect risk

triples.evidence_text: Tonmya (fibromyalgia): Based on animal data, Tonmya may increase the risk of neural tube defects when used two weeks before conception and through the first trimester. Because neural tube development happens early, often before pregnancy is recognized, avoid Tonmya during this window. Your healthcare provider should do a pregnancy test before you start Tonmya, and you should use effective contraception during treatment and for two weeks after the final dose. 3

Small published reports suggest cyclobenzaprine passes into breast milk in low amounts, but there is no information on effects on a breastfed baby or on milk supply. Talk with your healthcare provider about the benefits of breastfeeding alongside your need for this medicine. 2,3

triples.entity_2: 2.8 mg sublingually once daily at bedtime for 14 days
triples.evidence_text: Tonmya sublingual tablets (fibromyalgia): The recommended starting dose of Tonmya is 2.8 mg (1 sublingual tablet) once daily at bedtime for the first 14 days, then increases to the target dose of 5.6 mg (2 sublingual tablets) once daily at bedtime from day 15 onward. The maximum is 5.6 mg once daily. In adults 65 and older and in people with mild liver impairment, the maximum is 2.8 mg once daily at bedtime, and Tonmya is not recommended with moderate or severe liver impairment. 3

However, cyclobenzaprine has a similar structure to tricyclic antidepressants, and it is a recognized cause of false positive results on tricyclic antidepressant immunoassays, including urine immunoassays. Tests for tricyclic antidepressants are not part of routine drugs-of-abuse screening. 5

qualifiers.risk: greater impairment of thinking and reactions

triples.evidence_text: Avoid driving or hazardous activity until you know how cyclobenzaprine will affect you. It can impair your thinking and reactions, and this effect is stronger with alcohol or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking cyclobenzaprine. 1,2,3

With Tonmya, because it dissolves under the tongue, the most common side effects involve the mouth: reduced feeling or numbness in the mouth (23%), mouth discomfort, abnormal taste, tingling, mouth pain, and canker sores, along with sleepiness, fatigue, and dry mouth. Mouth-related effects usually begin within minutes of a dose and most resolve within an hour. Moistening your mouth with sips of water before dosing reduces the risk of numbness. Tell your healthcare provider if mouth effects are severe. 3
